ko_meaning: 일정한 지역에 사는 사람의 수
ko_meaning_en: The number of people living in a certain area

example.ko: 서울의 인구는 점점 줄어들고 있다.
example.roman: Seourui ingu-neun jeomjeom jureodeulgo itda.
example.en: Seoul's population is gradually decreasing.

form.q_en: Pick the adjective used with 인구 for 'a large population'.
form.why: A population is 많다 (large) or 적다 (small). 넓다 is for space, 비싸다 for price, 길다 for length.

ko_meaning: 한 도시나 나라에 살면서 권리와 의무를 가진 사람
ko_meaning_en: A person who lives in a city or country and has rights and duties

example.ko: 많은 시민들이 공원에서 축제를 즐겼어요.
example.roman: Maneun simindeuri gongwoneseo chukjereul jeulgyeosseoyo.
example.en: Many citizens enjoyed the festival in the park.

tokens.note: 들 = plural, 이 marks the subject

form.q_en: Pick the right form: 'The city must listen to citizens' opinions.'
form.why: 듣다 is ㄷ-irregular: 듣 + 어야 → 들어야. 들려야 comes from 들리다 (to be heard), which takes no object.

ko_meaning: 한 나라를 이루는 사람들
ko_meaning_en: The people who make up a country

example.ko: 모든 국민은 세금을 낼 의무가 있다.
example.roman: Modeun gungmineun segeumeul nael uimuga itda.
example.en: Every citizen has a duty to pay taxes.

form.q_en: Pick the particle: 'The president made a promise to the people.'
form.why: 에게 marks the person you promise or speak to. 국민 ends in a consonant, so 로 would have to be 으로, and 을/에서 do not fit here.

ko_meaning: 비슷한 나이에 태어나 같은 시대를 사는 사람들
ko_meaning_en: People born around the same time who live in the same era

example.ko: 젊은 세대는 주로 온라인으로 뉴스를 본다.
example.roman: Jeolmeun sedae-neun juro ollaineuro nyuseureul bonda.
example.en: The younger generation mostly watches the news online.

form.q_en: Pick the word that makes '-는 ___이다' mean 'tend to'.
form.why: -는 편이다 means 'tend to'. 척 needs 하다 (-는 척하다 = pretend), and 대로/만큼 do not form this pattern.

ko_meaning: 어떤 기준으로 나눈 땅의 한 부분
ko_meaning_en: One part of land divided by some standard

example.ko: 이 지역에는 오래된 한옥이 많아요.
example.roman: I jiyeogeneun oraedoen hanogi manayo.
example.en: There are many old hanok houses in this area.

tokens.note: 에 marks where something is; 는 adds the topic
past modifier: has been around a long time

form.q_en: Pick the particle for where the houses are.
form.why: Where something exists takes 에 (here 에는 as topic). 을 marks an object, 으로 a direction, and after a consonant 'and' is 과, not 와.

ko_meaning: 사람이 많이 살고 건물과 회사가 많은 큰 곳
ko_meaning_en: A big place where many people live, with many buildings and companies

example.ko: 도시에 살면 교통이 편리한 반면에 공기가 나쁘다.
example.roman: Dosi-e salmyeon gyotongi pyeollihan banmyeone gonggiga nappeuda.
example.en: If you live in a city, transportation is convenient, but the air is bad.

form.q_en: Pick the connector that shows contrast.
form.why: -(으)ㄴ 반면에 contrasts two facts. 덕분에 gives a good cause, 때문에 needs -기 here (편리하기 때문에), and -(으)ㄴ 김에 means 'while you are at it'.

ko_meaning: 농사를 지으며 사는 사람들이 많은 마을
ko_meaning_en: A village where many people live by farming

example.ko: 주말마다 농촌에 가서 일을 도와요.
example.roman: Jumalmada nongchone gaseo ireul dowayo.
example.en: Every weekend I go to the countryside and help with the work.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 돕다.
form.why: 돕다 is ㅂ-irregular and, like 곱다, becomes 도와요 (not 도워요). 돕아요/돕어요 keep the ㅂ, which is wrong.

ko_meaning: 한 사회에서 노인의 비율이 점점 높아지는 것
ko_meaning_en: The share of elderly people in a society gradually getting higher

example.ko: 고령화가 빠르게 진행되면서 노인 복지가 중요해졌다.
example.roman: Goryeonghwa-ga ppareuge jinhaengdoemyeonseo noin bokjiga jungyohaejyeotda.
example.en: As population aging progresses quickly, welfare for the elderly has become important.

tokens.note: -게 turns an adjective into an adverb

form.q_en: Pick the form meaning 'has become important'.
form.why: -아/어지다 shows a change: 중요하 + 여지다 → 중요해지다, past 중요해졌다. The other forms are not used.

ko_meaning: 아이를 적게 낳는 것
ko_meaning_en: Having few babies

example.ko: 저출산 문제를 해결하기 위해 정부가 여러 정책을 만들었다.
example.roman: Jeochulsan munjereul haegyeolhagi wihae jeongbuga yeoreo jeongchaegeul mandeureotda.
example.en: The government made several policies to solve the low birth rate problem.

tokens.note: noun used like an adjective before 문제

form.q_en: Pick the verb that goes with 문제 to mean 'solve the problem'.
form.why: 문제를 해결하다 = solve a problem. 발생하다 (occur) takes no object, and 낭비하다/배출하다 (waste/emit) do not fit.

ko_meaning: 부모와 결혼하지 않은 자녀로만 이루어진 가족
ko_meaning_en: A family made up only of parents and their unmarried children

example.ko: 요즘은 핵가족이 대부분이라서 명절에도 집이 조용해요.
example.roman: Yojeumeun haekgajogi daebubuniraseo myeongjeoredo jibi joyonghaeyo.
example.en: These days most families are nuclear families, so homes are quiet even on holidays.

form.q_en: Pick the ending meaning 'because (it) is'.
form.ko: 요즘은 핵가족이 대부분___ 명절에도 집이 조용해요.
form.why: 대부분 ends in a consonant, so 'because it is' is 이라서 (라서 follows a vowel). 이랑 means 'and/with' and 에서 'at/from'.

ko_meaning: 이유 없이 사람을 다르게 대하고 무시하는 것
ko_meaning_en: Treating people differently and badly without a good reason

example.ko: 나이나 성별에 따른 차별은 없어져야 한다.
example.roman: Naina seongbyeore ttareun chabyeoreun eopseojyeoya handa.
example.en: Discrimination based on age or gender must disappear.

form.q_en: Pick the verb: 'He faced discrimination because he was a foreigner.'
form.why: 차별을 받다 (or 당하다) = to be discriminated against. 얻다/가지다/걸다 do not go with 차별.

ko_meaning: 모든 사람이 차별 없이 똑같은 권리를 가지는 것
ko_meaning_en: All people having the same rights without discrimination

example.ko: 남녀 평등을 위해 많은 사람들이 노력해 왔어요.
example.roman: Namnyeo pyeongdeungeul wihae maneun saramdeuri noryeokae wasseoyo.
example.en: Many people have worked hard for equality between men and women.

tokens.note: -아/어 오다 = have been doing up to now

form.q_en: Pick the correct plain written form.
form.why: 평등하다 is an adjective, so its plain form stays 평등하다. Only action verbs take -ㄴ다/는다.

ko_meaning: 서로 생각이 달라서 사이가 나빠지는 것
ko_meaning_en: A relationship getting worse because people think differently

example.ko: 세대 간의 갈등을 줄이려면 대화가 필요하다.
example.roman: Sedae ganui galdeungeul juriryeomyeon daehwaga piryohada.
example.en: To reduce conflict between generations, conversation is needed.

form.q_en: Pick the verb: 'A conflict arose between the two people.'
form.why: 갈등이 생기다 = a conflict arises. 태어나다 is for babies, 만들다 needs an object, and 열리다 is for doors or events.

ko_meaning: 법을 지키지 않는 나쁜 행동
ko_meaning_en: A bad act that breaks the law

example.ko: 이 지역은 범죄가 적어서 밤에도 안전한 편이다.
example.roman: I jiyeogeun beomjoe-ga jeogeoseo bamedo anjeonhan pyeonida.
example.en: This area has little crime, so it is fairly safe even at night.

form.q_en: Pick the verb that goes with 범죄 for 'commit a crime'.
form.why: 범죄를 저지르다 = commit a crime. Solving, preventing or discovering a crime would not get him arrested (잡히다 = be caught).

ko_meaning: 일할 능력과 뜻이 있지만 직업이 없는 상태
ko_meaning_en: Having no job even though you are able and willing to work

example.ko: 경제가 나빠지면서 실업 문제가 심해졌다.
example.roman: Gyeongje-ga nappajimyeonseo sireop munjega simhaejyeotda.
example.en: As the economy got worse, the unemployment problem became serious.

form.q_en: Pick the ending for 'unemployment rate'.
form.why: After a consonant other than ㄴ, 'rate' is 률: 실업률. 율 follows a vowel or ㄴ, and 실업자 (the unemployed) cannot 'rise'.

ko_meaning: 신문이나 인터넷 뉴스에 나오는 글
ko_meaning_en: A piece of writing in a newspaper or online news

example.ko: 오늘 아침에 환경에 관한 기사를 읽었어요.
example.roman: Oneul achime hwangyeonge gwanhan gisa-reul ilgeosseoyo.
example.en: This morning I read an article about the environment.

tokens.note: N에 관한 = about N (before a noun)

form.q_en: Pick the form of 'about' that goes before a noun.
form.why: Before a noun, use the modifier 에 관한. 에 관해 modifies a verb, 관하다 takes 에 (not 을), and 관하는 is not used.

ko_meaning: 신문이나 방송에서 뉴스를 모으고 쓰는 사람
ko_meaning_en: A person who gathers and writes news for newspapers or broadcasting

example.ko: 기자들이 사고 현장에서 사람들을 인터뷰하고 있다.
example.roman: Gijadeuri sago hyeonjangeseo saramdeureul inteobyuhago itda.
example.en: Reporters are interviewing people at the scene of the accident.

form.q_en: Pick the verb that goes with 질문 'ask a question'.
form.why: 질문을 하다 = ask a question. 주다/보다/타다 do not go with 질문.

ko_meaning: 신문, 방송 등을 통해 사실을 알리고 의견을 말하는 것
ko_meaning_en: Informing people of facts and giving opinions through newspapers, broadcasts, etc.

example.ko: 그 사건은 언론의 큰 관심을 받았다.
example.roman: Geu sageoneun eollonui keun gwansimeul badatda.
example.en: The incident received a lot of media attention.

form.q_en: Pick the verb: 'The incident received a lot of media attention.'
form.why: 관심을 받다 = receive attention. 관심을 주다/보이다 is what the one paying attention does, and 관심을 하다 is not used.

ko_meaning: 신문이나 방송에서 새로운 소식을 널리 알리다
ko_meaning_en: To make new news widely known in newspapers or broadcasts

example.ko: 언론은 사실을 정확하게 보도해야 한다.
example.roman: Eolloneun sasireul jeonghwakage bodohaeya handa.
example.en: The press must report the facts accurately.

form.q_en: Pick the passive form: 'The incident was widely reported on the news yesterday.'
form.why: The incident is what gets reported, so use the passive 보도되다. 보도했다 would make the incident the reporter.

ko_meaning: 사회에서 일어난 특별하거나 문제가 되는 일
ko_meaning_en: A special or problematic thing that happens in society

example.ko: 경찰은 그 사건의 원인을 아직 밝히지 못했다.
example.roman: Gyeongchareun geu sageonui wonineul ajik balkiji motaetda.
example.en: The police have not yet revealed the cause of the incident.

form.q_en: Pick the verb: 'A big incident happened in this neighborhood last night.'
form.why: 사건이 일어나다 (or 발생하다) = an incident happens. 생산하다/만들다/열다 need an object.

ko_meaning: 어떤 일이나 문제가 생기다
ko_meaning_en: For something or a problem to happen

example.ko: 어젯밤 도로에서 큰 교통사고가 발생했다.
example.roman: Eojetbam doroeseo keun gyotongsagoga balsaenghaetda.
example.en: A big traffic accident occurred on the road last night.

form.q_en: Pick the right form: 'A fire broke out at the factory.'
form.why: 발생하다 already means 'to happen', so 화재가 발생했다. 발생시키다 needs an object, and the other two forms are not used.

ko_meaning: 어떤 일을 자세히 알아보다
ko_meaning_en: To look into something in detail

example.ko: 회사는 직원들의 만족도를 조사하기로 했어요.
example.roman: Hoesa-neun jigwondeurui manjokdoreul josahagiro haesseoyo.
example.en: The company decided to survey employee satisfaction.

form.q_en: Pick the right form: 'The police are investigating the cause of the accident.'
form.why: The police do the investigating and 원인을 is the object, so use the active 조사하고 있다. 조사되다/조사받다 are passive.

ko_meaning: 사람이 다치거나 물건이 망가져서 생긴 나쁜 결과
ko_meaning_en: A bad result from people getting hurt or things being broken

example.ko: 태풍 때문에 농촌 지역의 피해가 컸다.
example.roman: Taepung ttaemune nongchon jiyeogui pihae-ga keotda.
example.en: Rural areas suffered heavy damage because of the typhoon.

form.q_en: Pick the verb that goes with 피해 'suffer damage'.
form.why: 피해를 입다 = suffer damage. 입다 also means 'wear clothes', but 쓰다/신다/끼다 never go with 피해.

ko_meaning: 어떤 일이 생기게 한 이유
ko_meaning_en: The reason that made something happen

example.ko: 스트레스는 여러 질병의 원인이 될 수 있어요.
example.roman: Seuteureseu-neun yeoreo jilbyeongui wonini doel su isseoyo.
example.en: Stress can be a cause of various illnesses.

form.q_en: Pick the particle that goes with 되다.
form.ko: 스트레스는 질병의 원인___ 될 수 있어요.
form.why: 되다 takes 이/가 for what something becomes: 원인이 되다. 원인 ends in a consonant, so 이.

ko_meaning: 어떤 문제를 해결하기 위한 방법이나 계획
ko_meaning_en: A method or plan to solve a problem

example.ko: 정부는 미세먼지 문제에 대한 대책을 발표했다.
example.roman: Jeongbu-neun misemeonji munje-e daehan daechaegeul balpyohaetda.
example.en: The government announced measures against the fine dust problem.

tokens.note: N에 대한 = about N (before a noun)

form.q_en: Pick the verb that goes with 대책 'draw up measures'.
form.ko: 홍수 피해를 막기 위해 대책을 ___ 한다.
form.why: 대책을 세우다 = draw up measures. 서다/일어나다/올라가다 take no object.

ko_meaning: 한 지역에서 오랫동안 나타나는 날씨의 특징
ko_meaning_en: The usual weather pattern of a region over a long time

example.ko: 제주도는 기후가 따뜻해서 겨울에도 꽃이 핀다.
example.roman: Jejudo-neun gihu-ga ttatteutaeseo gyeouredo kkochi pinda.
example.en: Jeju Island has a warm climate, so flowers bloom even in winter.

form.q_en: Which word fits 'Today the ___ is clear and warm'?
form.why: 날씨 is the weather on a given day; 기후 is the long-term pattern of a region, so it is not 'clear today'.

ko_meaning: 지구의 온도가 점점 높아지는 현상
ko_meaning_en: The Earth's temperature gradually rising

example.ko: 지구 온난화 때문에 여름이 점점 더워지고 있어요.
example.roman: Jigu onnanhwa ttaemune yeoreumi jeomjeom deowojigo isseoyo.
example.en: Because of global warming, summers are getting hotter.

form.q_en: Pick the form meaning 'getting hotter'.
form.ko: 지구 온난화 때문에 여름이 점점 ___ 있어요.
form.why: 덥다 is ㅂ-irregular: 덥 + 어지다 → 더워지다. 더워하다 describes a person feeling hot, not the season.

ko_meaning: 나무나 석유 등에 들어 있고, 탈 때 공기 중으로 나오는 물질
ko_meaning_en: A substance in wood, oil, etc. that goes into the air when they burn

example.ko: 탄소 배출을 줄이기 위해 전기차를 타는 사람이 늘었다.
example.roman: Tanso baechureul jurigi wihae jeongichareul taneun sarami neureotda.
example.en: More people drive electric cars to reduce carbon emissions.

form.q_en: Pick the word for 'carbon emissions'.
form.why: 탄소 배출 = carbon emissions. You cannot 'reduce carbon saving' (절약), and 발명/수입 (invention/import) do not fit.

ko_meaning: 기계를 움직이거나 사람이 활동하는 데 필요한 힘
ko_meaning_en: The power needed to run machines or for people to be active

example.ko: 태양 에너지는 환경을 오염시키지 않는다.
example.roman: Taeyang eneoji-neun hwangyeongeul oyeomsikiji anneunda.
example.en: Solar energy does not pollute the environment.

form.q_en: Pick the form: 'A factory that uses a lot of energy pollutes the air.'
form.why: The factory makes the air dirty, so use the causative 오염시키다 with an object. 오염되다 is passive and 오염하다 is not used.

ko_meaning: 사람의 생활이나 경제에 쓰이는 물, 석유, 나무 같은 것
ko_meaning_en: Things like water, oil and wood that are used for daily life and the economy

example.ko: 자원이 부족한 나라일수록 기술이 중요하다.
example.roman: Jawoni bujokan narailsurok gisuri jungyohada.
example.en: The fewer resources a country has, the more important technology is.

form.q_en: Pick the correct plain written form.
form.why: 부족하다 is an adjective, so its plain form takes no -ㄴ다. 모자르다 is a misspelling of 모자라다, and 적다 stays 적다.

ko_meaning: 동물, 식물과 그것들이 사는 환경을 모두 합친 것
ko_meaning_en: All the animals and plants and the environment they live in, taken together

example.ko: 강물이 오염되면 생태계가 파괴될 수 있다.
example.roman: Gangmuri oyeomdoemyeon saengtaegye-ga pagoedoel su itda.
example.en: If river water is polluted, the ecosystem can be destroyed.

form.q_en: Pick the passive form: 'the ecosystem can be destroyed'.
form.why: The ecosystem is what gets destroyed, so the passive 파괴되다 is needed. 파괴하다/파괴시키다 need an object.

ko_meaning: 동물이나 식물의 한 종류가 모두 죽어서 없어지는 것
ko_meaning_en: A kind of animal or plant all dying out and disappearing

example.ko: 호랑이는 한국에서 오래전에 멸종되었다고 한다.
example.roman: Horangi-neun hangugeseo oraejeone myeoljongdoeeotdago handa.
example.en: They say tigers went extinct in Korea a long time ago.

form.q_en: Pick the word that completes 'in danger of extinction'.
form.why: 멸종 위기 = danger of extinction; 위기에 놓이다 = be in a crisis. 위험한 is a modifier, 위해 means 'for', and 위치 means 'location'.

ko_meaning: 오랫동안 비가 오지 않아 땅이 마르는 것
ko_meaning_en: The ground drying out because it does not rain for a long time

example.ko: 올해는 가뭄이 심해서 농사를 짓기 어려웠다.
example.roman: Olhae-neun gamumi simhaeseo nongsareul jitgi eoryeowotda.
example.en: The drought was severe this year, so farming was difficult.

form.q_en: Pick the verb: 'A drought set in because it did not rain.'
form.why: 가뭄이 들다 = a drought sets in. 내리다 is for rain or snow, 불다 for wind, and 떨어지다 for falling things.

ko_meaning: 비가 많이 와서 강물이 넘치는 것
ko_meaning_en: River water overflowing because of heavy rain

example.ko: 장마철에는 홍수가 나지 않도록 준비해야 한다.
example.roman: Jangmacheoreneun hongsu-ga naji antorok junbihaeya handa.
example.en: In the rainy season, we must prepare so that floods do not happen.

form.q_en: Pick the verb: 'There was a flood because it rained a lot yesterday.'
form.why: 홍수가 나다 = a flood happens. 불다 is for wind, 뜨다 for the sun or moon, and 켜지다 for lights.

ko_meaning: 땅속의 힘 때문에 땅이 흔들리는 것
ko_meaning_en: The ground shaking because of forces under the earth

example.ko: 지진이 발생하면 책상 아래로 들어가야 한다.
example.roman: Jijini balsaenghamyeon chaeksang arae-ro deureogaya handa.
example.en: When an earthquake occurs, you should get under a desk.

form.q_en: Pick the passive form: 'The building shook hard because of the earthquake.'
form.why: The building was shaken, so use the passive 흔들리다. 흔들다 needs an object (someone shakes something).

ko_meaning: 돈이나 물건, 시간 등을 아껴서 쓰다
ko_meaning_en: To use money, things or time carefully so as not to waste them

example.ko: 전기를 절약하려고 안 쓰는 불은 꼭 끈다.
example.roman: Jeongireul jeoryakaryeogo an sseuneun bureun kkok kkeunda.
example.en: To save electricity, I always turn off lights I'm not using.

form.q_en: Pick the plain written present form of 끄다.
form.why: 끄다 ends in a vowel, so the plain present is 끄 + ㄴ다 → 끈다. -는다 follows a consonant.

ko_meaning: 돈이나 시간, 물건을 필요 없는 곳에 많이 쓰다
ko_meaning_en: To use a lot of money, time or things where they are not needed

example.ko: 쓸데없는 일에 시간을 낭비하지 마세요.
example.roman: Sseuldeeomneun ire siganeul nangbihaji maseyo.
example.en: Don't waste time on useless things.

form.q_en: Pick the ending for 'Please don't waste'.
form.why: A negative request is -지 마세요. -고/-게/-면 cannot come before 말다 here.

ko_meaning: 안에 있는 것을 밖으로 내보내다
ko_meaning_en: To send out something that was inside

example.ko: 자동차는 많은 양의 탄소를 배출한다.
example.roman: Jadongcha-neun maneun yangui tansoreul baechulhanda.
example.en: Cars emit a large amount of carbon.

form.q_en: Pick the passive form: 'Smoke from the factory is released into the sky.'
form.why: The smoke is what is let out, so use the passive 배출되다. 배출한다 would need an object.

ko_meaning: 수나 양, 크기를 원래보다 작게 하다
ko_meaning_en: To make a number, amount or size smaller than before

example.ko: 건강을 위해서 단 음식을 줄이려고 해요.
example.roman: Geongangeul wihaeseo dan eumsigeul juriryeogo haeyo.
example.en: I'm trying to cut down on sweet food for my health.

form.q_en: Pick the form that takes an object: 'cut down on sweet food'.
form.why: 줄이다 (to reduce something) takes an object; 줄어들다 (to decrease) does not. 줄이 + 려고 → 줄이려고.

ko_meaning: 새로운 물건이나 기술을 만들거나 더 좋게 만드는 것
ko_meaning_en: Making a new product or technology, or making it better

example.ko: 이 회사는 새로운 스마트폰 개발에 많은 돈을 투자했다.
example.roman: I hoesa-neun saeroun seumateupon gaebare maneun doneul tujahaetda.
example.en: This company invested a lot of money in developing a new smartphone.

form.q_en: Pick the word: 'The company developed a new medicine.'
form.why: 개발하다 = develop (make) something new and takes an object. 발전하다 (progress), 발생하다 (occur) and 출발하다 (depart) take no object.

ko_meaning: 물건이나 서비스를 만들고 사고파는 모든 활동
ko_meaning_en: All activities of making, buying and selling goods and services

example.ko: 요즘 경제가 어려워서 취직하기가 쉽지 않아요.
example.roman: Yojeum gyeongje-ga eoryeowoseo chwijikagiga swipji anayo.
example.en: The economy is tough these days, so getting a job isn't easy.

tokens.note: -기 makes a verb into a noun

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 어렵다.
form.why: 어렵다 is ㅂ-irregular: ㅂ becomes 우, so 어렵 + 어서 → 어려워서.

ko_meaning: 여러 가지 물건과 서비스의 평균적인 가격
ko_meaning_en: The average price of goods and services

example.ko: 물가가 너무 올라서 장 보기가 무서워요.
example.roman: Mulga-ga neomu ollaseo jang bogiga museowoyo.
example.en: Prices have gone up so much that I'm scared to go grocery shopping.

tokens.note: 장(을) 보다 = to go grocery shopping

form.q_en: Pick the verb for prices rising.
form.why: 물가가 오르다 = prices rise (오르 + 았다 → 올랐다). 타다/커지다/길어지다 do not go with 물가.

ko_meaning: 돈이나 물건, 시간 등을 써서 없애는 것
ko_meaning_en: Using up money, goods, time, etc.

example.ko: 여름에는 에너지 소비가 크게 증가한다.
example.roman: Yeoreumeneun eneoji sobi-ga keuge jeunggahanda.
example.en: Energy consumption increases greatly in summer.

form.q_en: Pick the active form: 'People don't spend money, so the economy is struggling.'
form.why: People spend (소비하다) money, which is the object. 소비되다 is passive, and 소비시키다 means making someone else spend.

ko_meaning: 사람에게 필요한 물건을 만들어 내는 것
ko_meaning_en: Making things that people need

example.ko: 이 공장에서는 하루에 자동차 천 대를 생산한다.
example.roman: I gongjangeseoneun harue jadongcha cheon daereul saengsanhanda.
example.en: This factory produces a thousand cars a day.

form.q_en: Pick the counter for cars.
form.ko: 이 공장은 하루에 자동차 천 ___를 생산한다.
form.why: 대 counts cars and machines. 마리 is for animals, 권 for books, and 잔 for cups.

ko_meaning: 다른 나라에서 물건을 사 들여오는 것. 또는 일을 해서 번 돈
ko_meaning_en: Buying goods in from another country; also money earned from work

example.ko: 한국은 바나나를 대부분 외국에서 수입해요.
example.roman: Hangugeun banana-reul daebubun oegugeseo suipaeyo.
example.en: Korea imports most of its bananas from abroad.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for comparing (수입 = income here).
form.ko: 이번 달은 수입___ 지출이 더 많았다.
form.why: 보다 marks what you compare against, used with 더: 'spending was more than income'. 처럼/만큼 mean 'like/as much as' and clash with 더.

ko_meaning: 다른 나라에 물건이나 기술을 팔아 내보내는 것
ko_meaning_en: Selling goods or technology to other countries

example.ko: 한국 드라마가 여러 나라에 수출되고 있다.
example.roman: Hanguk deurama-ga yeoreo nara-e suchuldoego itda.
example.en: Korean dramas are being exported to many countries.

form.q_en: Korea sells many cars abroad. Which word fits?
form.why: 수출하다 = export (sell to other countries). 수입하다 is the opposite (buy from abroad), and 소비/구매 do not go with 외국에.

ko_meaning: 이익을 얻으려고 돈이나 시간, 노력을 들이는 것
ko_meaning_en: Putting in money, time or effort to get a profit

example.ko: 건강에 투자하는 것은 결코 낭비가 아니다.
example.roman: Geongange tujahaneun geoseun gyeolko nangbi-ga anida.
example.en: Investing in your health is never a waste.

form.q_en: Pick the ending that goes with 결코 'never'.
form.why: 결코 is always followed by a negative, so 낭비가 아니다 (is never a waste).

ko_meaning: 돈을 벌기 위해 물건이나 서비스를 만들어 파는 회사
ko_meaning_en: A company that makes and sells goods or services to earn money

example.ko: 많은 기업들이 인공지능 기술에 투자하고 있다.
example.roman: Maneun gieopdeuri ingongjineung gisure tujahago itda.
example.en: Many companies are investing in AI technology.

form.q_en: Pick the verb: 'He founded a company at a young age.'
form.why: 기업을 세우다 = found a company. 서다/일어나다 take no object, and 타다 is for vehicles.

ko_meaning: 물건을 팔거나 일을 해서 얻은 돈이나 도움
ko_meaning_en: Money or benefit gained from selling or working

example.ko: 올해 회사는 작년보다 두 배의 이익을 얻었다.
example.roman: Olhae hoesa-neun jangnyeonboda du baeui iigeul eodeotda.
example.en: This year the company made twice as much profit as last year.

form.q_en: Pick the verb that goes with 이익 'make a profit'.
form.ko: 이 가게는 한 달에 백만 원의 이익을 ___.
form.why: 이익을 내다 = make a profit. 빼다 (subtract), 끄다 (turn off) and 건너다 (cross) do not fit.

ko_meaning: 돈이나 물건을 잃어서 생긴 나쁜 결과
ko_meaning_en: A bad result from losing money or things

example.ko: 싸게 팔면 손해를 볼 수도 있어요.
example.roman: Ssage palmyeon sonhae-reul bol sudo isseoyo.
example.en: If you sell it cheaply, you might lose money.

form.q_en: Pick the verb that goes with 손해 'suffer a loss'.
form.why: 손해를 보다 = suffer a loss (also 이익을 보다 = gain). 만들다/읽다/찍다 do not go with 손해.

ko_meaning: 일을 해서 일정한 기간 동안 번 돈
ko_meaning_en: Money earned from work over a certain period

example.ko: 소득이 높을수록 세금을 많이 낸다.
example.roman: Sodeugi nopeulsurok segeumeul mani naenda.
example.en: The higher your income, the more tax you pay.

form.q_en: Pick the word that describes 'low-income people'.
form.why: Income is 높다/낮다 (or 많다/적다). 적다 is an adjective, so its modifier is 적은, not 적는; 짧다/좁다 are for length and space.

ko_meaning: 나라가 일을 하기 위해 국민에게서 받는 돈
ko_meaning_en: Money the country collects from its people to do its work

example.ko: 세금으로 도로와 학교를 짓는다.
example.roman: Segeumeuro dorowa hakgyoreul jinneunda.
example.en: Roads and schools are built with taxes.

form.q_en: Pick the verb that goes with 세금 'pay taxes'.
form.why: 세금을 내다 = pay taxes. 주다/사다/타다 do not go with 세금.

ko_meaning: 어떤 일을 하는 데 드는 돈
ko_meaning_en: The money needed to do something

example.ko: 유학 비용이 생각보다 많이 들어서 걱정이에요.
example.roman: Yuhak biyongi saenggakboda mani deureoseo geokjeongieyo.
example.en: Studying abroad costs more than I thought, so I'm worried.

form.q_en: Pick the verb: 'Moving cost a lot of money.'
form.why: Money and cost take 들다 (비용이 들다); time takes 걸리다. 쓰다 would need an object.

ko_meaning: 앞으로 쓸 돈을 미리 계산해서 정한 계획
ko_meaning_en: A plan made by working out in advance the money you will spend

example.ko: 여행 예산이 부족해서 숙소를 싼 곳으로 바꿨어요.
example.roman: Yeohaeng yesani bujokaeseo suksoreul ssan goseuro bakkwosseoyo.
example.en: My travel budget was short, so I changed to a cheaper place to stay.

form.q_en: Pick the verb that goes with 예산 'draw up a budget'.
form.why: 예산을 짜다 (or 세우다) = draw up a budget. 입다/끄다/찍다 do not go with 예산.

ko_meaning: 어떤 목적을 위해 돈을 쓰는 것. 또는 그 돈
ko_meaning_en: Spending money for a purpose; or that money

example.ko: 이번 달에는 식비 지출을 줄이기로 했다.
example.roman: Ibeon dareneun sikbi jichureul jurigiro haetda.
example.en: This month I decided to cut my food spending.

form.q_en: Which word fits: 'My salary is the same, but I have a lot of ___, so I'm short of money'?
form.why: Only spending (지출) makes you short of money. 수입/이익/소득 are money coming in.

ko_meaning: 돈을 내고 물건이나 서비스를 사서 쓰는 사람
ko_meaning_en: A person who pays for and uses goods or services

example.ko: 소비자들은 가격보다 품질을 더 중요하게 생각한다.
example.roman: Sobijadeureun gagyeokboda pumjireul deo jungyohage saenggakanda.
example.en: Consumers consider quality more important than price.

form.q_en: Which word fits: 'The person who makes things is the producer; the person who buys them is the ___.'
form.ko: 물건을 만드는 사람은 생산자이고 사는 사람은 ___이다.
form.why: 소비자 (consumer) buys and uses goods; 생산자 (producer) makes them. 기자 and 작가 are a reporter and a writer.

ko_meaning: 사고팔기 위해 만든 물건
ko_meaning_en: Goods made to be bought and sold

example.ko: 이 상품은 인터넷에서만 살 수 있어요.
example.roman: I sangpumeun inteoneseseoman sal su isseoyo.
example.en: This product can only be bought online.

form.q_en: Pick the verb meaning 'launched (a product)'.
form.why: 출시하다 = put a product on the market. 출발하다 (depart), 출근하다 (go to work) and 출장하다 (go on a business trip) take no product.

ko_meaning: 물건의 좋고 나쁜 정도
ko_meaning_en: How good or bad a product is

example.ko: 이 가게 물건은 값은 싸지만 품질이 좋지 않다.
example.roman: I gage mulgeoneun gapseun ssajiman pumjiri jochi anta.
example.en: Things at this store are cheap, but the quality is not good.

form.q_en: Pick the expression meaning 'not only ... but also'.
form.ko: 이 노트북은 품질이 좋을 ___ 가격도 싸다.
form.why: -(으)ㄹ 뿐만 아니라 = not only ... but also. 반면에 and 대신에 need -(으)ㄴ/-는 before them, and 때문에 needs -기.

ko_meaning: 다른 사람을 위해 도움을 주는 일. 또는 가게에서 공짜로 더 주는 것
ko_meaning_en: Work that helps others; also something a shop gives you extra for free

example.ko: 그 식당은 음식도 맛있고 서비스도 친절해요.
example.roman: Geu sikdangeun eumsikdo masitgo seobiseu-do chinjeolhaeyo.
example.en: That restaurant has delicious food and friendly service.

form.q_en: Which word means 'on the house' (free extra)?
form.why: In Korean shops 서비스 also means something given free. 유료 means 'paid', 중고 'second-hand', and 세일 'sale'.

ko_meaning: 물건을 돈을 주고 사다
ko_meaning_en: To buy goods by paying money

example.ko: 요즘은 온라인으로 상품을 구매하는 사람이 많다.
example.roman: Yojeumeun ollaineuro sangpumeul gumaehaneun sarami manta.
example.en: These days many people buy products online.

form.q_en: Pick the past modifier: 'Products you have bought cannot be refunded.'
form.why: -(으)ㄴ is the past modifier for verbs: 구매한 상품 = a product (already) bought. -(으)ㄹ is future, and 구매해서 cannot modify a noun.

ko_meaning: 해마다 지키며 즐기는 전통적인 날
ko_meaning_en: A traditional day celebrated every year

example.ko: 명절마다 고향에 가는 사람들로 길이 혼잡하다.
example.roman: Myeongjeolmada gohyange ganeun saramdeullo giri honjapada.
example.en: Every holiday, the roads are crowded with people heading to their hometowns.

form.q_en: Pick the particle meaning 'every'.
form.why: 마다 = every: 명절마다 = every holiday. 만큼/처럼/보다 compare things.

ko_meaning: 음력으로 새해의 첫날. 한국의 큰 명절
ko_meaning_en: The first day of the new year by the lunar calendar; a big Korean holiday

example.ko: 설날에는 가족들이 모여서 떡국을 먹어요.
example.roman: Seollareneun gajokdeuri moyeoseo tteokgugeul meogeoyo.
example.en: On Lunar New Year's Day, families gather and eat rice cake soup.

form.q_en: Pick the humble verb for bowing to elders.
form.why: To elders (께) you use the humble 드리다: 세배를 드리다. 주다 is for equals or juniors, and 받다 is what the elders do.

ko_meaning: 음력 8월 15일. 가을에 송편을 만들어 먹는 한국의 큰 명절
ko_meaning_en: The 15th day of the 8th lunar month; a big Korean autumn holiday when people make and eat songpyeon

example.ko: 추석에는 송편을 만들고 보름달을 본다.
example.roman: Chuseogeneun songpyeoneul mandeulgo boreumdareul bonda.
example.en: On Chuseok, people make songpyeon and look at the full moon.

form.q_en: Pick the verb that goes with a holiday: 'Have a nice Chuseok with your family.'
form.why: 명절을 보내다 = spend a holiday, so 추석 잘 보내세요. 가다/받다/드시다 do not go with 추석.

ko_meaning: 옛날부터 한 사회에 전해 내려오는 생활 습관
ko_meaning_en: Ways of living handed down in a society from long ago

example.ko: 나라마다 결혼에 관한 풍습이 조금씩 다르다.
example.roman: Naramada gyeolhone gwanhan pungseubi jogeumssik dareuda.
example.en: Wedding customs differ a little from country to country.

form.q_en: Pick the verb: 'The villagers still keep the old customs.'
form.ko: 그 마을 사람들은 지금도 옛날 풍습을 ___ 있다.
form.why: 풍습을 지키다 = keep (follow) a custom. 막다 (block), 잡다 (catch) and 끄다 (turn off) do not fit.

ko_meaning: 돌아가신 가족을 기억하며 음식을 차려 놓고 인사하는 일
ko_meaning_en: Setting out food and bowing to remember family members who have passed away

example.ko: 우리 집은 일 년에 세 번 제사를 지낸다.
example.roman: Uri jibeun il lyeone se beon jesa-reul jinaenda.
example.en: My family holds ancestral rites three times a year.

tokens.note: 제사를 지내다 = hold an ancestral rite

form.q_en: Pick the verb that goes with 제사.
form.ko: 우리 가족은 일 년에 한 번 할아버지 제사를 ___.
form.why: 제사를 지내다 = hold an ancestral rite. 보내다 is for time or holidays, and 입다/만들다 do not go with 제사.

ko_meaning: 한국의 전통 옷
ko_meaning_en: Korea's traditional clothes

example.ko: 경복궁에 한복을 입고 가면 입장료가 무료이다.
example.roman: Gyeongbokgunge hanbogeul ipgo gamyeon ipjangnyoga muryoida.
example.en: If you go to Gyeongbokgung Palace wearing hanbok, admission is free.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 아름답다.
form.why: 아름답다 is ㅂ-irregular: ㅂ becomes 우, so 아름다워요. 아름다와요 is an old spelling that is no longer correct.

ko_meaning: 한국의 전통 방식으로 지은 집
ko_meaning_en: A house built in Korea's traditional way

example.ko: 한옥은 여름에 시원하고 겨울에 따뜻한 편이다.
example.roman: Hanogeun yeoreume siwonhago gyeoure ttatteutan pyeonida.
example.en: Hanok houses are fairly cool in summer and warm in winter.

form.q_en: Pick the modifier for an adjective before 편이다.
form.why: With adjectives, 편이다 takes -(으)ㄴ: 따뜻한 편이다. -는 is for action verbs.

en: to be unique; to be inherent
ko_meaning: 어떤 것만 원래부터 특별히 가지고 있다
ko_meaning_en: To be something that only one thing has, from the beginning

example.ko: 각 나라에는 고유한 문화가 있다.
example.roman: Gak nara-eneun goyuhan munhwa-ga itda.
example.en: Each country has its own unique culture.

form.q_en: Pick the modifier form of 고유하다.
form.why: 고유하다 is an adjective, so before a noun it takes -ㄴ: 고유한 음식. -는 is for action verbs.

ko_meaning: 옛날 사람들이 남긴 물건
ko_meaning_en: Objects left behind by people of the past

example.ko: 박물관에서 신라 시대의 유물을 감상했어요.
example.roman: Bangmulgwaneseo silla sidae-ui yumureul gamsanghaesseoyo.
example.en: I looked at relics from the Silla period at the museum.

form.q_en: Pick the passive form: 'This relic was found in the ground 100 years ago.'
form.ko: 이 유물은 백 년 전에 땅속에서 ___.
form.why: The relic is what was found, so use the passive 발견되다. 발견했다 would make the relic the finder.

ko_meaning: 옛날 사람들이 살았던 곳이나 건물이 남아 있는 자리
ko_meaning_en: A place where traces or buildings of people from long ago remain

example.ko: 경주에는 역사 유적이 많아서 해마다 관광객이 찾아온다.
example.roman: Gyeongju-eneun yeoksa yujeogi manaseo haemada gwangwanggaegi chajaonda.
example.en: Gyeongju has many historic sites, so tourists visit every year.

form.q_en: Pick the word that forms 'historic site' with 지 (place).
form.why: 유적지 = a historic site. 유물 are objects, so there is no 유물지; 작품지/전통지 are not words.

ko_meaning: 그림, 음악, 춤처럼 아름다움을 표현하는 활동
ko_meaning_en: Activities that express beauty, like painting, music and dance

example.ko: 어릴 때부터 예술에 관심이 많았어요.
example.roman: Eoril ttaebuteo yesure gwansimi manasseoyo.
example.en: I've been very interested in art since I was young.

form.q_en: Pick the particle used with 관심이 많다.
form.why: 관심이 있다/많다 takes 에 for the topic of interest: 예술에 관심이 많다.

ko_meaning: 그림, 소설, 음악처럼 예술가가 만든 것
ko_meaning_en: Something an artist creates, such as a painting, novel or music

example.ko: 이 작품은 작가가 십 년 동안 그린 그림이다.
example.roman: I jakpumeun jakga-ga sim nyeon dongan geurin geurimida.
example.en: This work is a painting the artist worked on for ten years.

form.q_en: Pick the verb: 'That painter left many works.'
form.why: 작품을 남기다 = leave works behind (takes an object). 남다 (remain) and 나가다 take no object, and 놓치다 means 'miss'.

ko_meaning: 소설, 시, 그림 같은 예술 작품을 만드는 사람
ko_meaning_en: A person who makes works of art such as novels, poems or paintings

example.ko: 제가 가장 좋아하는 작가의 새 책이 나왔어요.
example.roman: Je-ga gajang joahaneun jakga-ui sae chaegi nawasseoyo.
example.en: A new book by my favorite writer came out.

form.q_en: Pick the polite way to address the author.
form.why: 작가님 is the polite title for a writer. 작가씨 sounds rude, 작가야 is for close friends or children, and 께서 is a subject particle, not a way to call someone.

ko_meaning: 여러 사람이 볼 수 있도록 물건을 한곳에 늘어놓다
ko_meaning_en: To set things out in one place so that many people can see them

example.ko: 이 미술관은 젊은 작가들의 그림을 전시하고 있다.
example.roman: I misulgwaneun jeolmeun jakgadeurui geurimeul jeonsihago itda.
example.en: This art museum is exhibiting paintings by young artists.

form.q_en: Pick the passive form: 'That painting is on display at the museum now.'
form.why: The painting is what is displayed, so use the passive 전시되다 + -어 있다 (a resulting state).

ko_meaning: 음악, 그림, 영화 같은 예술 작품을 즐기며 느끼다
ko_meaning_en: To enjoy and take in works of art such as music, paintings or films

example.ko: 주말에는 집에서 클래식 음악을 감상하는 편이에요.
example.roman: Jumareneun jibeseo keullaesik eumageul gamsanghaneun pyeonieyo.
example.en: On weekends I usually listen to classical music at home.

form.q_en: Which word fits: 'My hobby is watching films'?
form.why: 영화 감상 / 음악 감상 = enjoying films / music, a common way to name a hobby. 조사/생산/배출 do not fit.

ko_meaning: 무엇을 만들거나 하는 방법이나 능력
ko_meaning_en: A method or ability for making or doing something

example.ko: 의료 기술이 발전하면서 사람들의 수명이 늘었다.
example.roman: Uiryo gisuri baljeonhamyeonseo saramdeurui sumyeongi neureotda.
example.en: As medical technology has advanced, people's lifespans have increased.

form.q_en: Pick the verb: 'I go to an academy to learn cooking skills.'
form.why: 기술을 배우다 = learn a skill. 입다/타다/마시다 do not go with 기술.

ko_meaning: 더 좋은 상태로 나아가는 것
ko_meaning_en: Moving forward to a better state

example.ko: 인터넷의 발전으로 생활이 많이 편리해졌다.
example.roman: Inteonesui baljeoneuro saenghwari mani pyeollihaejyeotda.
example.en: Thanks to the development of the internet, life has become much more convenient.

form.q_en: Pick the word: 'The Korean economy developed quickly.'
form.why: 발전하다 = develop, progress. 발생하다 means 'occur', and 발견하다/발명하다 (discover/invent) need an object.

ko_meaning: 사람처럼 생각하고 배울 수 있게 만든 컴퓨터 기술
ko_meaning_en: Computer technology made to think and learn like a person

example.ko: 인공지능이 사람의 일자리를 빼앗을까 봐 걱정하는 사람이 많다.
example.roman: Ingongjineungi saramui iljarireul ppaeaseulkka bwa geokjeonghaneun sarami manta.
example.en: Many people worry that AI might take people's jobs.

form.q_en: Pick the ending meaning 'worried that ... might'.
form.why: -(으)ㄹ까 봐 = (worried) that something might happen. -(으)ㄹ수록 means 'the more', and 잃을뿐/잃을려고 do not fit here.

ko_meaning: 인터넷과 여러 가지 앱을 쓸 수 있는 핸드폰
ko_meaning_en: A mobile phone that can use the internet and many apps

example.ko: 자기 전에 스마트폰을 오래 보면 잠을 잘 못 잔다.
example.roman: Jagi jeone seumateuponeul orae bomyeon jameul jal mot janda.
example.en: If you look at your smartphone for a long time before bed, you can't sleep well.

form.q_en: Pick the word for 'can't (sleep well)'.
form.ko: 스마트폰을 오래 보면 잠을 잘 ___ 잔다.
form.why: 못 before a verb means 'cannot': 잘 못 잔다. 없/말/아니 cannot stand before a verb like this.

ko_meaning: 스마트폰이나 컴퓨터처럼 어떤 일을 하는 데 쓰는 기계
ko_meaning_en: A machine used for some job, like a smartphone or a computer

example.ko: 아이들이 전자 기기를 너무 오래 사용하면 눈이 나빠진다.
example.roman: Aideuri jeonja gigi-reul neomu orae sayonghamyeon nuni nappajinda.
example.en: If children use electronic devices too long, their eyesight gets worse.

form.q_en: Pick the form meaning 'gets worse'.
form.why: 나쁘다 + -아/어지다 → 나빠지다 (ㅡ drops), plain present 나빠진다.

ko_meaning: 이름, 주소, 전화번호처럼 한 사람을 알아볼 수 있는 정보
ko_meaning_en: Information that can identify a person, such as name, address and phone number

example.ko: 모르는 사람에게 개인정보를 알려 주면 안 돼요.
example.roman: Moreuneun saramege gaeinjeongbo-reul allyeo jumyeon an dwaeyo.
example.en: You must not give your personal information to strangers.

tokens.note: 안 돼요 = it is not allowed

form.q_en: Pick the verb: 'Companies must protect customers' personal information.'
form.why: 개인정보를 보호하다 = protect personal information. 낭비하다/배출하다/수출하다 (waste/emit/export) do not fit.

ko_meaning: 중요한 정보나 장소를 위험으로부터 안전하게 지키는 것
ko_meaning_en: Keeping important information or places safe from danger

example.ko: 보안을 위해 비밀번호를 자주 바꾸는 것이 좋다.
example.roman: Boaneul wihae bimilbeonhoreul jaju bakkuneun geosi jota.
example.en: For security, it is good to change your password often.

tokens.note: -는 것이 좋다 = it is good to; sounds like [조타]

form.q_en: Pick the particle that goes with 위해.
form.why: 위하다 takes an object: N을/를 위해 = for N. 보안 ends in a consonant, so 을.

ko_meaning: 인터넷 등에서 필요한 정보를 찾다
ko_meaning_en: To look for needed information on the internet, etc.

example.ko: 모르는 단어가 있으면 인터넷으로 검색해 보세요.
example.roman: Moreuneun daneo-ga isseumyeon inteoneseuro geomsaekae boseyo.
example.en: If there's a word you don't know, try searching for it online.

form.q_en: Pick the active form: 'I searched for that restaurant online.'
form.why: I am the one searching and 식당을 is the object, so use the active 검색하다. 검색되다 is passive.

ko_meaning: 컴퓨터나 핸드폰에 자료를 넣어 두다. 또는 물건을 모아서 보관하다
ko_meaning_en: To keep data in a computer or phone; also to collect and keep things

example.ko: 중요한 파일은 꼭 저장해 두어야 한다.
example.roman: Jungyohan paireun kkok jeojanghae dueoya handa.
example.en: You must be sure to save important files.

tokens.note: -아/어 두다 = do and keep it that way

form.q_en: Pick the ending meaning 'so that'.
form.why: -도록 = so that: 잊지 않도록 = so that I won't forget. 않 + 면서 would have to be 않으면서, and the others do not give a purpose.

ko_meaning: 기계나 프로그램을 쓸 수 있도록 자리에 놓거나 넣다
ko_meaning_en: To put a machine or program in place so it can be used

example.ko: 방에 에어컨을 설치하려면 돈이 꽤 든다.
example.roman: Bange eeokeoneul seolchiharyeomyeon doni kkwae deunda.
example.en: Installing an air conditioner in the room costs quite a lot of money.

form.q_en: Pick the plain written present form of 들다.
form.why: With ㄹ-stem verbs the ㄹ drops before ㄴ: 들 + ㄴ다 → 든다.

ko_meaning: 인터넷에 연결되어 있는 상태
ko_meaning_en: Being connected to the internet

example.ko: 이 강의는 온라인으로만 들을 수 있다.
example.roman: I gangui-neun ollaineuroman deureul su itda.
example.en: This lecture can only be taken online.

form.q_en: Pick the past form of 듣다.
form.why: 듣다 is ㄷ-irregular: 듣 + 었다 → 들었다. 들렀다 comes from 들르다 (stop by).

ko_meaning: 정보를 숫자로 바꾸어 처리하는 방식
ko_meaning_en: A way of handling information by turning it into numbers

example.ko: 요즘은 종이 신문보다 디지털 뉴스를 보는 사람이 많다.
example.roman: Yojeumeun jongi sinmunboda dijiteol nyuseureul boneun sarami manta.
example.en: These days more people read digital news than paper newspapers.

form.q_en: Pick the word that combines with 화 ('-ization') to mean 'digitize'.
form.why: 디지털화하다 = digitize. 편리화/품질화/가뭄화 are not words.

ko_meaning: 기계가 사람의 손을 쓰지 않고 스스로 움직이는 것
ko_meaning_en: A machine working by itself without people's hands

example.ko: 이 문은 사람이 가까이 가면 자동으로 열린다.
example.roman: I muneun sarami gakkai gamyeon jadongeuro yeollinda.
example.en: This door opens automatically when a person comes close.

tokens.note: passive of 열다; plain written present

form.q_en: Pick the passive form: 'the door opens (by itself)'.
form.why: The door opens by itself, so use the passive 열리다 → 열린다. 연다 (from 열다) needs someone to open something.

ko_meaning: 지금까지 없던 새로운 물건이나 방법을 처음 만들어 내는 것
ko_meaning_en: Making a new thing or method for the first time

example.ko: 전화기의 발명은 사람들의 생활을 크게 바꾸었다.
example.roman: Jeonhwagiui balmyeongeun saramdeurui saenghwareul keuge bakkueotda.
example.en: The invention of the telephone greatly changed people's lives.

form.q_en: Pick the word for finding something that already existed.
form.ko: 없던 것을 처음 만드는 것은 발명이고, 이미 있던 것을 처음 찾아내는 것은 ___이다.
form.why: 발견 = discovery (finding what already existed); 발명 = invention (making something new). 발전/발생/개발 mean progress/occurrence/development.

ko_meaning: 쓰기 쉽고 이용하기 좋다
ko_meaning_en: Easy and handy to use

example.ko: 지하철역이 가까워서 출퇴근하기가 편리하다.
example.roman: Jihacheollyeogi gakkawoseo chultoegeunhagiga pyeollihada.
example.en: The subway station is close, so commuting is convenient.

form.q_en: Which word fits: 'Transportation here is inconvenient, so you really need a car'?
form.ko: 이 동네는 교통이 ___ 차가 꼭 필요하다.
form.why: 불편하다 is the opposite of 편리하다. Only inconvenient transportation explains needing a car.

ko_meaning: 자기 생각이 옳다고 강하게 말하는 것. 또는 그 생각
ko_meaning_en: Strongly saying that your opinion is right; or that opinion

example.ko: 그의 주장은 근거가 부족해서 설득력이 없다.
example.roman: Geuui jujangeun geungeo-ga bujokaeseo seoldeungnyeogi eopda.
example.en: His argument lacks evidence, so it isn't persuasive.

form.q_en: Pick the verb that goes with 주장 'put forward an argument'.
form.why: 주장을 펼치다 (or 하다) = put forward an argument. 입다/걸다/닫다 do not go with 주장.

ko_meaning: 어떤 생각이나 의견이 옳다는 것을 보여 주는 이유
ko_meaning_en: A reason that shows an idea or opinion is right

example.ko: 자신의 의견을 말할 때는 근거를 들어야 한다.
example.roman: Jasinui uigyeoneul malhal ttae-neun geungeo-reul deureoya handa.
example.en: When you state your opinion, you should give reasons.

form.q_en: Pick the right form of 들다 in 'give grounds'.
form.ko: 토론할 때는 주장과 함께 근거를 ___ 한다.
form.why: 근거를 들다 = give grounds; 들 + 어야 → 들어야. 들려야 is from 들리다 (be heard), and 드러야 is a misspelling.

ko_meaning: 다른 사람의 의견이나 계획이 옳다고 보고 따르는 것
ko_meaning_en: Thinking someone else's opinion or plan is right and going along with it

example.ko: 회의에서 많은 사람이 새 규칙에 찬성했다.
example.roman: Hoeuieseo maneun sarami sae gyuchige chanseonghaetda.
example.en: At the meeting, many people agreed with the new rule.

form.q_en: Pick the particle used with 찬성하다.
form.why: 찬성하다 takes 에 for what you agree with. 규칙 ends in a consonant, so 'and' would be 과, and 규칙이 would make the rule the one agreeing.

ko_meaning: 어떤 의견이나 계획을 따르지 않는 것. 또는 방향이 서로 거꾸로인 것
ko_meaning_en: Not going along with an opinion or plan; also being in the opposite direction

example.ko: 부모님의 반대에도 불구하고 그는 결혼을 했다.
example.roman: Bumonimui bandae-edo bulguhago geuneun gyeolhoneul haetda.
example.en: Despite his parents' opposition, he got married.

form.q_en: Which word also means 'opposite (side)'?
form.why: 반대 also means 'opposite': 반대쪽 = the opposite side. 찬성/주장/입장 cannot describe a direction.

ko_meaning: 어떤 문제에 대해 가지는 생각이나 태도
ko_meaning_en: The view or attitude you have on an issue

example.ko: 이 문제에 대한 정부의 입장은 분명하다.
example.roman: I munje-e daehan jeongbu-ui ipjangeun bunmyeonghada.
example.en: The government's position on this issue is clear.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'from (someone's) point of view'.
form.why: N의 입장에서 = from N's point of view. 입장 ends in a consonant, so 로/와 would have to be 으로/과.

ko_meaning: 다른 사람의 의견과 같은 생각을 가지다
ko_meaning_en: To have the same view as someone else's opinion

example.ko: 저는 그 의견에 완전히 동의합니다.
example.roman: Jeo-neun geu uigyeone wanjeonhi donguihamnida.
example.en: I completely agree with that opinion.

form.q_en: Pick the correct formal ending for a debate.
form.why: The formal ending after a vowel stem is -ㅂ니다: 동의하 + ㅂ니다 → 동의합니다. -습니다 follows a consonant, and 요 is never added to -다.

ko_meaning: 다른 사람의 의견이나 주장이 틀렸다고 맞서서 말하다
ko_meaning_en: To argue back that someone's opinion or claim is wrong

example.ko: 그는 상대방의 주장을 논리적으로 반박했다.
example.roman: Geuneun sangdaebangui jujangeul nollijeogeuro banbakaetda.
example.en: He logically rebutted the other person's argument.

form.q_en: Pick the particle used with 반박하다.
form.why: 반박하다 takes an object: 주장을 반박하다. 주장이 would make the argument the one rebutting.

ko_meaning: 어떤 것을 특별히 중요하다고 힘주어 말하다
ko_meaning_en: To say strongly that something is especially important

example.ko: 선생님은 매일 복습하는 것이 중요하다고 강조하셨다.
example.roman: Seonsaengnimeun maeil bokseupaneun geosi jungyohadago gangjohasyeotda.
example.en: The teacher stressed that reviewing every day is important.

form.q_en: Pick the indirect-speech ending for an adjective.
form.why: Adjectives take -다고 in indirect speech: 중요하다고. -는다고 is for action verbs, -라고 for nouns or commands, and -냐고 for questions.

ko_meaning: 어떤 의견이나 계획을 내놓다
ko_meaning_en: To put forward an idea or plan

example.ko: 친구가 주말에 같이 등산을 가자고 제안했다.
example.roman: Chingu-ga jumare gachi deungsaneul gajago jeanhaetda.
example.en: My friend suggested going hiking together on the weekend.

form.q_en: Pick the indirect-speech ending for 'let's'.
form.why: A suggestion (let's ...) is reported with -자고: 가자고 제안했다. -냐고 reports a question, and 가다고/가는다고 are wrong forms.

ko_meaning: 잘못이나 문제가 되는 점을 집어서 말하다
ko_meaning_en: To point out a mistake or problem

example.ko: 선배가 내 보고서의 문제점을 지적해 주었다.
example.roman: Seonbae-ga nae bogoseo-ui munjejeomeul jijeokae jueotda.
example.en: A senior colleague pointed out the problems in my report for me.

form.q_en: Pick the helping verb: someone did it for me.
form.why: -아/어 주다 = someone does something for me. -아/어 드리다 is for doing something for a superior, and 받다/보내다 do not work as helping verbs here.
